evangelism.deadline: 1 December (Discipleship Plan to the district superintendent); approved plans reach the conference by 1 March; cheques are usually mailed by 31 March
evangelism.how: Each year the church board writes a Discipleship Plan on the conference form (events and estimated costs for each GROW phase: Prepare, Plant, Cultivate, Harvest, Preserve), stating its monthly evangelism budget and the amount requested from district evangelism funds; the pastor sends it to the district superintendent (not the conference office) by 1 December.
conditions: Every church must submit a Discipleship Plan, even if it asks for no district funds.
The plan shows the church board approval date and the church's monthly evangelism budget.

At the first district meeting of the year (usually January) the district pastors agree how to divide the district's evangelism funds; the superintendent signs each plan with the amount approved (possibly $0).
Plans that miss the schedule do not receive evangelism funds.

Separate route: MAP Pooled Resource Funds (from 25% of statewide Michigan Advance Partners offerings) can pay up to 100% of a 'unique' (new, uncommon, outside-the-box) outreach or evangelism project. The church's lay advisory representative (not the pastor) applies online at least four weeks before a Lay Advisory Statewide Coordinating Committee meeting; 2026 deadlines were 1 March, 26 July and 8 November; funds depend on availability.
evangelism.report: Before the series, record it on the conference's Evangelistic Series Record form (one per church per series: dates, days, number of meetings, location). Afterwards, complete the Evangelistic Series Follow-Up Survey: opening-night attendance, non-Adventists on opening night, non-Adventists attending at least once and at least half the meetings, new interests, decisions to join, baptisms and ongoing interests.
